records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes Task Scheduler as executing tasks when configured criteria are met. Registered tasks can launch programs or scripts; enumeration does not justify disabling, editing, or running tasks, and task identity/privileges must be preserved.

records.title: KNOWNFOLDERID
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes KNOWNFOLDERID constants as GUIDs for standard system-registered folders. Resolve paths through the OS API rather than assuming a localized or redirected profile path; folder ACLs and redirection still need runtime checks.

records.title: Run and RunOnce Registry Keys
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn states Run/RunOnce keys start programs at user logon. Removing an entry can disable user or system functionality; preserve exact hive, name, type, command, policy context, and conflict-aware rollback, and protect security/driver/hardware entries.

records.title: System Informer
records.evidence: The public repository describes a multi-purpose system monitor/debugger and malware-detection tool and displays an MIT license link. Exact license text, privileged components, process-control behavior, release provenance, and redistribution requirements were not reviewed.

records.title: ChangeServiceConfigW
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn API page opened and explicitly describes changing a service's configuration parameters. Service identity, required access rights, driver/security-service protections, boot impact, backup/rollback, and UAC behavior must be validated in a disposable Windows environment before any implementation.

records.title: Task Scheduler Schema
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn says the XML schema defines valid task-registration XML used with ITaskFolder.RegisterTask. Schema-valid XML can still request dangerous triggers, principals, actions, or privileges; do not import/register arbitrary task XML.

records.title: Win11Debloat
records.evidence: The public repository describes a PowerShell script for removing preinstalled apps, disabling telemetry, and other Windows 10/11 changes and displays an MIT license link. No script was copied or run; source safety, exact effects, policy conflicts, license text, and rollback behavior were not reviewed.

records.title: winget uninstall
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes the winget uninstall command as uninstalling a specified application. Package identifiers, source selection, interactive behavior, dependency effects, and reinstallation/rollback must be explicit; never pass arbitrary command text or uninstall without approval.

records.title: Reparse Points
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn overview opened describing file/directory reparse points. Traversal and cleanup must account for links, junctions, and other reparse tags to avoid escaping an approved root or deleting unintended data; the exact file-operation flags require implementation tests.

records.title: SHEmptyRecycleBinW
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn explicitly describes this Shell API as emptying the Recycle Bin on a specified drive. This can irreversibly destroy user-recoverable files and must not run as an automatic cleanup or optimization; no invocation was made.

records.title: Path.GetTempPath
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn API page opened and lists net-8.0 support. The returned temporary directory is environment-dependent and does not establish that a file is safe to delete; validate ownership, canonical path, reparse points, age, and application ownership.

records.title: Directory.EnumerateFiles
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn API page opened and lists net-8.0 support. Enumeration can encounter access, I/O, and path changes; safe cleanup must bound traversal, avoid following reparse points, handle partial enumeration explicitly, and never convert errors into success.

records.title: SHA256 Class
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn API page opened and lists net-8.0 support. SHA-256 can produce a content digest but an untrusted digest does not authenticate a publisher or prove package provenance; signature/trust verification is separate.

records.title: Czkawka duplicate file tools
records.evidence: The public repository describes a cross-platform app for finding duplicate/empty folders and similar media and displays an MIT license link. Exact source behavior, deletion safeguards, license terms, pinned version, dependencies, and suitability for integration were not reviewed.

records.title: Optimize-Volume
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn redirected to the Storage module page with a WindowsServer2025-ps moniker and Windows 11 product metadata. Volume optimization is a mutating maintenance operation whose behavior depends on media, filesystem, and selected mode; exact option semantics, device support, elevation, interruption, and verification require disposable-system tests.

records.title: Native Wifi
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes Native Wifi APIs for configuring, connecting to, and disconnecting from wireless networks. Network profile changes can disrupt connectivity and expose credentials; this overview does not validate any particular operation, consent flow, rollback, or supported adapter.

records.title: IP Helper API
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes IP Helper as supporting retrieval and modification of local network configuration. It is a broad API catalog; changing routes, interfaces, or addresses is high-impact and requires an individually validated action, consent, and connectivity recovery.

records.title: Set-DnsClientServerAddress
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn redirected to the DNS Client module page with a WindowsServer2025-ps moniker and Windows 11 product metadata. Setting DNS server addresses changes network configuration and can break name resolution; interface selection, existing state backup, policy/permission handling, verification, rollback, and offline behavior are unvalidated.

records.title: Microsoft Media Foundation
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn Media Foundation SDK overview opened. Device capture requires explicit user consent, privacy settings, device-specific error handling, and safe release of media resources; an SDK overview is not evidence that a webcam can be opened or is available.

records.title: Enumerating Video Capture Devices
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn how-to describes enumerating video-capture devices and creating a device instance. Enumeration is not consent to activate a camera; privacy controls, device ownership, hotplug, unsupported formats, and no-capture diagnostics must be tested.

records.title: Microsoft SBOM Tool
records.evidence: The public Microsoft repository describes an SPDX 2.2-compatible SBOM generator and displays an MIT license link. Exact tool version, license text, input completeness, package detection coverage, and verification of generated SBOMs remain unreviewed.

records.title: System Restore
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes APIs for setting restore points and monitoring changes to support system rollback. Restore-point creation is not a substitute for application-owned per-action backups and does not guarantee every application/configuration change is reversible; no restore point was created.

records.title: SQLite Online Backup API
records.evidence: SQLite documentation explains that the online backup API produces a consistent snapshot while avoiding pitfalls of copying a live database file, including WAL/locking and crash corruption. This is relevant to database backup, not backup of Windows configuration; restore integrity and transaction coordination still need tests.

records.title: Microsoft DiskSpd
records.evidence: The public Microsoft repository describes DiskSpd as a storage load generator/performance test tool and displays an MIT license link. It can impose substantial I/O load and alter test conditions; do not run on a user's machine or treat synthetic throughput as a universal optimization score.

records.title: BenchmarkDotNet overview
records.evidence: BenchmarkDotNet documentation states support for .NET Framework/Core, Mono, NativeAOT, and Windows/Linux/macOS and shows Release-mode microbenchmarking. Package/version/license review and reproducible application-level workload design are separate; microbenchmarks do not establish game FPS improvements.

records.title: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite overview
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn overview for Microsoft.Data.Sqlite opened. Exact package version, native SQLite build, SQLite feature availability, provider settings, durability configuration, and license/transitive-dependency review remain separate tasks.

records.title: UI Automation Overview
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes UI Automation as a Windows accessibility framework for supported applications, including WPF. The .NET Framework overview is not a current app test plan; selectors, control semantics, end-to-end bindings, error states, and accessibility behavior still require executable UI tests.

records.title: Testing in .NET
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn testing overview opened. It describes concepts and tooling, not HyperBoostX test evidence; test suites, isolation, assertion coverage, environment, exact commands, and results must be recorded from this repository's actual runs.

records.title: NamedPipeServerStream Class
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn API reference resolves to System.IO.Pipes.NamedPipeServerStream for .NET 8 and includes .NET 8 in its ranged monikers (the page currently defaults to .NET 11). The stream API alone does not establish peer authentication, restrictive ACLs, message validation, replay protection, least privilege, or secure broker behavior.

records.title: Named Pipe Security and Access Rights
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes Windows security descriptors controlling access to both named-pipe client and server ends. Correct ACL construction, client identity verification, impersonation rules, service isolation, denial tests, and resistance to pipe squatting still require a concrete implementation and isolated Windows tests.

records.title: Auditing package dependencies for security vulnerabilities
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn describes NuGet package vulnerability auditing and acting on audit reports. Enabling restore-time auditing is not a completed security review; advisory data freshness, transitive/runtime/package coverage, severity policy, suppression governance, and actual CI results must be verified.

records.title: Create a .NET application with plugins
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn tutorial demonstrates plugin loading with AssemblyLoadContext and AssemblyDependencyResolver to isolate dependency resolution. Separate load contexts are not a security sandbox: executing a plugin in-process retains the host process trust and privileges; untrusted plugins need a separately designed process boundary and permissions.

records.title: Discord Rate Limits
records.evidence: Discord developer documentation says route/global limits vary and should not be hard-coded; clients should parse rate-limit response headers and respond appropriately. This informs a possible optional integration but does not establish consent, payload privacy, credential protection, network resilience, or live connectivity.

records.title: Discord Webhook Resource
records.evidence: Discord documents incoming webhook URLs/tokens as credentials that can post without a bot user. Any integration must treat the URL as a secret, obtain explicit consent for outbound data, preview/redact payloads, avoid logging it, and handle revocation/rate limits; no webhook was invoked.

records.title: XAML Resources Overview
records.evidence: Microsoft Learn explains reusable WPF XAML resources such as brushes and styles. Shared resources support consistent presentation but do not alone provide dynamic theme switching, high-DPI validation, accessibility, or localization.

records.title: Microsoft PowerToys
records.evidence: The public Microsoft PowerToys repository describes a Windows productivity/customization utilities collection and displays an MIT license link. This is a product/project reference, not an API or evidence of feature compatibility; no code was copied and license text/release provenance were not audited.

records.evidence: Microsoft Learn overview discusses WPF globalization/localization, automatic layout and satellite assemblies; the page identifies its service as dotnet-framework and dates to 2017.
